title: TCMS Onboard HMI Dashboard
excerpt: A fully simulated train management dashboard with real-time speed gauge, route tracking, alarm system, and vehicle diagnostics — built as a single-page HTML application.
description: Designed and built a complete HMI dashboard simulating an onboard TCMS for a regional train running Napoli–Salerno. Features include real-time speed gauge with arc rendering, station-by-station route progress, door status monitoring, traction/brake gauges, alarm management, and environmental data display. The simulation runs autonomously with realistic acceleration, braking, and station-stop cycles.
motivation: I wanted to demonstrate that a functional HMI prototype can be built rapidly with web technologies, without heavy frameworks — useful for rapid prototyping and stakeholder demos before committing to platform-specific toolchains.

title: F1 Miami GP — Race Replay Dashboard
excerpt: An interactive race replay that reconstructs the Miami Grand Prix from real telemetry data — track visualization, live standings, pit stops, and time-gap calculation, all in a single self-contained HTML file.
description: Built a Python pipeline that fetches real race data from the Jolpica/Ergast F1 API (lap times, positions, pit stops), processes it, and generates a fully interactive HTML dashboard. The dashboard renders the Miami International Autodrome from official SVG path data, places all 20 drivers as animated dots, and replays the race with accurate time gaps. Features include play/pause, speed control (1x to 30x), a timeline scrubber, live standings sidebar with real-time gap calculation, pit stop indicators, and leader glow effects.
motivation: I wanted to explore how far you can push a single-file web application for sports data visualization — no frameworks, no backend, just vanilla JS rendering real race data. The Python script handles the data engineering; the browser handles the storytelling.
